_comment: Declarative MCP inventory: released Git deployments, remote URL references, and machine-local registrations. Pi uses pi-mcp-adapter with built-in MCP disabled; it reads ~/.pi/agent/mcp.json and ~/.config/mcp/mcp.json. No secrets or org-specific values belong here.

servers.name: m365-personal-productivity
servers.description: Martin's personal Microsoft 365: Outlook calendar and mail (read + draft/create), Teams chat, SharePoint files, meeting transcripts, and mailbox organisation (categories, folders, filing)
servers._piPackageNote: Registers the checkout as a Pi package so the m365-tools skill it ships under skills/ is loaded. Claude hosts do not take packages; m365-martin tells them where to read the skill.
servers._supersedesNote: Older host keys for this same server, removed from every host on install so a machine does not end up with two registrations. 'm365' is the name this server had in Pi's mcp.json before the installer managed Pi.
servers._envNote: No secrets here. The server ships config.defaults.json with a non-secret tenant id; export M365_TENANT_ID before setup for a machine-local override, never commit a real tenant id. All write gates are ON by the owner's decision (all write functionality wanted; security engaged; separate app registration). Every send, delete and rule change still goes through the server's staged preview + confirm_action approval, so 'on' means 'ask', not 'execute silently'. These env gates are superseded by the per-tool always/ask/off policy file once feature F0 ships; set any of them to 'false' here to force a capability off on every host.
servers._dirNote: A deployment-only copy that the installer moves between tags. Never point this at the checkout you develop in: the installer refuses a checkout that is on a branch, and hosts would otherwise run whatever you last built. Develop in ~/source/... as usual; ship by releasing and re-running the installer.
servers._refNote: "latest" = the newest release tag (vX.Y.Z, no pre-release), resolved by scripts/resolve-release.sh after fetching. Put an exact tag here only to hold this server back. See RELEASES.md.

servers.name: memory
servers._buildNote: pnpm is pinned through npx so the build needs only node/npm, not a globally installed pnpm (Node 25+ no longer bundles corepack). Keep the version in step with packageManager in memory-mcp's package.json.
servers.description: Martin's second brain: three-tier markdown memory (core, archive, bank) over the local DailyDriver data repo, with a one-way publish path
servers._hostsNote: Pi only, matching how it was registered by hand before. Claude Desktop is planned as a later read surface; widen this list deliberately, since writes are enabled.
servers._requiresNote: DailyDriver is a private GitHub repository (never public). '01 - Setup Mac Environment.sh' clones it and writes ~/.config/memory-mcp/config.json before this installer runs; its content never enters this public repository. The installer warns if it is missing; the server refuses to start without it.
servers._envNote: MEMORY_ALLOW_WRITE=true keeps the posture it had when registered by hand; core writes are staged and confirmed; memory_record automatically captures attributed bank claims and authored archive decisions and the gate is only read from here, never from the settings file. MEMORY_REMOTE_ALLOWED=private-github acknowledges DailyDriver's private remote; set here first so the server-startup remote guard can ship without breaking hosts. env values are expanded with $HOME by the installer because GUI hosts do not expand variables.
servers._refNote: "latest" = the newest release tag (vX.Y.Z, no pre-release), resolved by scripts/resolve-release.sh after fetching. Put an exact tag here only to hold this server back. See RELEASES.md.

servers.name: confluent
servers.manualSetup: Install the approved Confluent npm release into $HOME/.local/share/mcp-confluent; create its machine-local config.yaml and register the stdio entry plus --config and reviewed --block-tools restrictions in the referenced registry. See MCP/README.md.

servers.name: atlassian
servers.manualSetup: Register the remote Atlassian URL locally in the referenced registry and complete interactive OAuth with the adapter. See MCP/README.md.

servers.name: datadog
servers.manualSetup: Configure the Datadog remote URL and OAuth locally in the referenced adapter registry; sign in interactively. See MCP/README.md.

servers.name: atlassian-rovo
servers.manualSetup: Configure the Rovo remote URL, OAuth and reviewed excludeTools locally in the referenced adapter registry; sign in interactively. Preserve this distinct name. See MCP/README.md.
